sources.entry: Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques by Jiawei Han, Micheline Kamber, and Jian Pei

summary.name: Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques
summary.one_liner: A 3rd edition (2011) textbook by Jiawei Han, Micheline Kamber, and Jian Pei covering data mining and knowledge discovery from data, from preprocessing and data warehousing through classification, clustering, and outlier detection.
use_cases: Learning data mining concepts for a university course
Looking up pseudo-code for classification or clustering algorithms
Understanding data warehousing and OLAP design
Preparing and cleaning data before mining
Background reading for data science practitioners
summary.what_it_does: The book covers data mining from basics to advanced topics. It starts with data objects, attribute types, statistical descriptions, visualization, and similarity measures. It then covers data preprocessing (cleaning, integration, reduction, transformation) and data warehousing with OLAP and data cube technology. Core chapters address frequent pattern and association mining, classification (decision trees, Bayes, rule-based, backpropagation, SVMs, lazy learners), and cluster analysis. Later chapters cover advanced pattern mining, advanced clustering, outlier detection, and research frontiers and applications. The page says it presents dozens of algorithms in pseudo-code.
notable: Presents dozens of algorithms in pseudo-code for large-scale projects
Covers advanced topics such as spatial, multimedia, time-series, text, and web data mining
Includes chapter-end exercises and bibliographic notes, per reviews
caveats: Print textbook listing; the page does not describe any software or platform
Readers are expected to have statistics, database, and programming background, per a review quote
